object: Graffito (adoration, proskynema), two lines of Meroitic very neatly executed, 40 x 4 cm; L., D., VI, Bl. 1, no. 1; rubbing in Burton MS. 25,650 f. 9, squeezes Lepsius and Borchardt, photos 476-477; Pls. XXXVIII-XXXIX
site: Philae, Gate of Hadrian: the doorway, in the thickness of the wall, north jamb (the only inscription there)

text_corpus: tewisti apote yebye tiSo woS pileqeteli nlw berkelo
notes: 2 stone lines; (2) printed before wos. Assembled from the table: A right column 'tewiseti :', A left column 'apote : yebye : tiso :'; section B row empty; C right column '(2)wos : pileqeteli :', C left column 'nlw : berkelo :', then 'end'. Description p. 45 (n64): the first two characters in each line are worn but can easily be restored; nearly identical with the inscription in the Colonnade. English (p. 51, n70): 'The adoration made by the envoy piously unto Isis in Philae.' Griffith: te-wisti = demotic t-wste 'the salutation, obeisance'; apote = 'envoy' (also in 95, 123, all neatly executed, perhaps by one person); the group ending -so (here tiso) means something like 'of, done by'; nlw + berkelo render 'piously (before)'. No query marks or sic in this row. Checked at 2.5-3.5x: the 3-shaped sign of tiso is the closed s of wos (not m or ẖ); berkelo has k (flat Z top, as in ksbñ), not p. ' | ' separates the parts of the text taken from the successive sections (A to E) of Griffith's Table of Seven Graffiti of Philae (p. 50); within a section the right-hand column is read before the left-hand one, and a section printed on several lines is joined; (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign; [...] his dots.

Griffith's queries (? over the sign): l of blyeso; y of mey; y of penylito; p of pẖrsetelo. Description pp. 47-48 (n66-n67): the stone has deteriorated; much of it, especially the lower lines, is very obscure, lightly engraved or worn down, but parallel passages help the reading greatly and few signs remain uncertain. English (pp. 51-52, n70-n71): 'The adoration made by (?) the khabkhen of the king, and qeren, the kin of the strategus of the water, remaining (?) before Isis in Philae and Isis in Tebawe; kin of the Agent of Isis and qeren of Isis, mey-mebaras of penay(l), mazek in Philae, maze in Pachoras, belonging to the kashbam of Isis' (cf. 111/15). Griffith: perite wost qoreñ wost = demotic p qrny n 3S p rt n 3S, 'the qeren of Isis, the Agent of Isis'; pelmos = strategus; pẖrse-telo (122/10) a place-name, Pachoras, probably modern Faras; 122 and 123 end in the same three words. Checked at 2.5-3.5x: m (hook and long straight descender) in yetmdelo, pelmos, mey, mebrse, mdek, mde; s (closed 3) in pelmos, wost, wos, ksbñ, blyeso; ẖ (angular top) in pẖrsetelo, matching Griffith's 'Phrs'; k (flat top) in mdek and ksbñ. notes: 2 stone lines; (2) printed before t. Assembled from the table: A right 'tewiseti :', A left 'a[s]y ye[bye] (2)t[iso]'; B '. . . . . qo' (the dots stand right of qo, so they are read first); C right 'wos', C left 'nlw', then 'end'. Griffith's queries (? over the sign): the restored s and the y of a[s]y, the e of ye[bye], the t of t[iso]; bye and iso are his restorations (after the parallel yebye : tiso of 121). Notes pp. 48-49 (n67-n68): much worn and injured, many round pittings, so no dividers marked except after the first word; the right-hand end of l. 2 is cut to pieces; l. 1: 'It seems hardly possible to read apote here. Nothing is recognizable after ye, and perhaps nothing more was engraved'; l. 2: traces in the first half, possibly left blank, 'at the beginning, however, t is fairly clear'; qo is followed by a space before the cross; of two cuttings at the top of the cross the second might be the remains of a sign, the first is not a Meroitic letter; no third line. The gate is late (perhaps Diocletian's fortifications), so the text is probably 4th century AD or later, the most northerly Meroitic inscription. English (p. 51): 'The adoration made by (?) the .... .... unto Isis.' Griffith: nlw ('before' ?) is used alone here. The 3-shaped restored sign of a[s]y and t[iso] is the closed s of wos.
